step1_figure.description: A common-source NMOS amplifier (M1) loaded by an active PMOS current source (M2) biased by the wide-swing bias generator (SUB_1, Fig. 20.43) via Vbias1, self-biased around saturation with a high-resistance feedback resistor R1 and AC-coupled input.

quiescent_current.description: DC bias/quiescent drain current through the common-source stage

equation.explanation: M2 acts as a current source biased from the beta-multiplier reference circuit (R=6.5k, Fig. 20.43) to supply Class-A bias current.
equation.assumptions: M1 and M2 in saturation; self-biasing feedback resistor R1 holds Vout = Vin at operating point.

sky130_expected.calculation: With R=6.5k in SUB_1 beta-multiplier and long-channel devices, reference current is ~20 uA; mirrored to PMOS load M2: I_D ≈ 20 uA.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Determined by the 6.5k resistor and device aspect ratios in the bias subcircuit.

equation.explanation: Voltage gain is the transconductance of input transistor M1 multiplied by the total output resistance (drain resistances of M1 and M2 in parallel).
equation.assumptions: Both M1 and M2 remain saturated; parasitic loads negligible at low frequency.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Active current source load provides high load impedance, significantly boosting voltage gain over diode-connected load.

output_resistance.description: Small-signal output resistance looking into node Vout

equation.explanation: Parallel combination of drain-to-source resistances of NMOS driver M1 and PMOS current source load M2.
equation.assumptions: No external load resistance connected; channel-length modulation dominates.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Driven by channel-length modulation parameters of SKY130 FETs at 1um gate length.

input_pole_frequency.description: Dominant input pole frequency determined by source resistance and Miller capacitance

equation.explanation: Pole formed by Rs (100 kOhm) and input capacitance augmented by Miller multiplication of Cgd1.
equation.assumptions: Miller approximation holds at the first pole frequency.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Large Miller multiplier from ~35 dB gain pushes the dominant input pole into the low-MHz region.

output_pole_frequency.description: Second pole frequency at the output node

equation.explanation: High-frequency pole formed by the total output node resistance and capacitance.
equation.assumptions: Output node capacitance dominated by device parasitic capacitances.

sky130_expected.calculation: Total output node parasitic C_out ≈ 20 fF, R_o ≈ 250 kOhm. f_out = 1 / (2*pi*250k*20fF) ≈ 31.8 MHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: With no external load capacitor, output pole sits near tens of MHz.

rhp_zero_frequency.description: Right-Half Plane (RHP) zero frequency from direct feedthrough via Cgd1

equation.explanation: Zero occurs when small-signal current through feedthrough capacitor Cgd1 cancels the transconductance current gm1*vgs.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Because gm is hundreds of uA/V and Cgd is a few fF, the RHP zero is well into the GHz range.

unity_gain_frequency.description: Frequency where voltage gain drops to 0 dB (unity gain)

equation.explanation: Gain-bandwidth product under dominant single-pole rolloff.
equation.assumptions: First-order rolloff between f_in and f_out.

sky130_expected.calculation: f_un ≈ 12 MHz * 58 ≈ 700 MHz (with second pole interaction, typical unity-gain frequency is ~200 MHz to 500 MHz).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Interactions between Miller pole and output pole shape the 0 dB crossover.

equation.explanation: Gain evaluated at 400 MHz to verify roll-off characteristics as presented in Ex. 21.3.
equation.assumptions: Operation in -20 dB/dec or -40 dB/dec rolloff region.

sky130_expected.calculation: At 400 MHz, well past the dominant pole (~12 MHz), gain has rolled off by ~30 dB from DC.
sky130_expected.reasoning: High-frequency attenuation due to Rs and internal parasitics.

slew_rate.description: Output slew rate when driving a 1 pF load capacitor

equation.explanation: Maximum rate of charging output capacitance set by the constant PMOS current source load.
equation.assumptions: M1 cuts off during negative input transition, forcing all M2 current into the load.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Class-A current limit of 20 uA directly determines the maximum charging rate.

step3_testbench.description: Comprehensive ngspice testbench for Common-Source amplifier with current-source load (Fig. 21.17): evaluates DC bias, AC frequency response (DC gain, dominant pole, unity gain, phase, 400 MHz magnitude), and transient slew rate with 1 pF capacitive load.
